Sparse Volume Textures (SVT) is a volume rendering technique in Unreal Engine 5 that renders large, sparse volumetric datasets (up to ~6 gigavoxels) by sampling data stored in sparse tiles within a large volume texture [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial][S3].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence. Source [S2] explicitly states that the technique was implemented in a custom build of Unreal Engine 5.4 and successfully rendered the Kolumbo dataset, which has a total resolution of approximately 6 billion voxels (4211 × 1501 × 935 ≈ 6 billion). Source [S1] and [S3] confirm that Sparse Volume Textures (SVT) are used within Unreal Engine for volume rendering (specifically via Heterogeneous Volumes) and involve sampling data stored in sparse structures (tiles/volumes).
